routes.description: Establish Christianity as the better moral foundation for society by connecting its truth claims and account of transcendent moral obligation to universal human dignity, protection of vulnerable people, and durable practices of sacrificial community and social flourishing.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds by explaining why Christian claims furnish an objective and socially actionable moral ground, why the incarnation and cross support equal dignity beyond contingent human preference, and why secular humanism cannot secure the same protections or benefits on its own premises.

motionBridge.description: Show that Christianity provides society a more secure and beneficial moral foundation than atheism or secular humanism.

centralBridges.description: Connect objective moral values and obligations to a true transcendent foundation that cannot be reduced to biology, preference, or social agreement.
Explain how divine identification with vulnerable humanity grounds equal dignity and protection even when human interests narrow the moral circle.
Connect intrinsic Christian commitment with durable communal practices and social benefits not fully explained by community participation alone.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Account for the persistence of sacred values and exclusionary group dynamics within nominally irreligious communities.
Explain Christianity's claimed historical role in forming norms of sacrifice by the strong for weak people and outsiders.

routes.description: Establish secular humanism as the better moral foundation for society by distinguishing it from bare atheism, grounding deliberation in shared human interests and well-being, and showing that community, moral revision, and protection from harm do not require supernatural premises.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds by presenting a usable human-centered standard for moral evaluation, showing how secular communities can reproduce relevant social goods, answering claims that dignity or obligation requires God, and demonstrating comparative advantages from revising harmful inherited doctrines.

motionBridge.description: Show that secular humanism offers society a more workable and corrigible moral foundation than Christianity while bare atheism need not supply a complete program.

centralBridges.description: Ground moral deliberation in shared concern for human beings and assess conduct through consequences for human well-being.
Show that invoking God neither resolves motivational disagreement nor establishes the truth or practical accessibility of the proposed moral foundation.
Explain how secular humanism can inherit useful traditions while correcting doctrines or practices that conflict with present human flourishing.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Establish that secular communities can sustain belonging, awe, higher commitments, sacrifice, and practical support without supernatural belief.
Explain how consequence-based moral reasoning can remain revisable while still criticizing exclusionary and oppressive social systems.

sections.title: Foundation, Truth, and Moral Objectivity
sections.rationale: The central metaphysical clash concerns whether moral truth and obligation require a nonmaterial Christian explanation or can begin from human interests without an additional divine premise.

sections.title: Human Dignity and the Moral Circle
sections.rationale: The comparative burdens turn substantially on whether universal protection for weak and excluded people is secured by divine identification with humanity or by human valuation and shared well-being.

sections.title: Community, Transcendence, and Social Flourishing
sections.rationale: Claims about health, resilience, generosity, belonging, awe, and higher commitments test whether Christianity supplies distinctive social goods or whether secular institutions can reproduce their operative causes.

sections.title: Moral Inheritance, Revision, and Social Consequences
sections.rationale: The motion requires comparing Christianity's claimed historical formation of humane norms with secular humanism's capacity to preserve useful ideas, reject harmful baggage, and revise judgments through their consequences.

sections.title: Atheism, Secular Humanism, and Public Practice
sections.rationale: Distinguishing bare atheism from secular humanism and examining disagreement, dogmatism, and shared premises determines what each position actually proposes as a workable social foundation.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: Removing God from public discourse does not remove religious impulses and may instead redirect them into heightened secular moralism, exclusion, anathemas, and ideological witch hunts.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Intrinsic religiosity is associated with broad personal and social flourishing, including health, happiness, resilience, family stability, charitable giving, volunteering, and blood donation.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: The distinctive benefits attributed to intrinsic religiosity arise not merely from community membership but from organizing one's most important decisions and whole life toward something higher and transcendent.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: Christian moral practice must be grounded in what is actually true about the world, with its practical success offered as an inference to Christianity's truth rather than as the source of that truth.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-03.proposition: Christianity reverses survival-of-the-fittest morality through the sacrifice of the strongest for the weakest and extends equal human dignity even to enemies and people who are weak, marginalized, ineffective, or maladaptive to survival.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: The incarnation grounds humanity's intrinsic dignity because God became vulnerable human flesh for weak and despised people, whereas elevating humanity without divine identification risks resting human exceptionalism on an unsupported assertion of power.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-10.proposition: Because human self-interest tends to narrow the moral circle, society needs a secure foundation that protects equal dignity and human rights for weak people regardless of capacity, attributes, or achievements.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-06.proposition: Christian teaching that the strong should sacrifice themselves to protect the weak shaped Western moral sensibilities so that Nazism's opposite principle was recognizable as evil and worthy of resistance.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-09.proposition: Objective moral values require a nonmaterial explanation because ethical obligations are distinct from and cannot be reduced to biological survival, natural facts, material causes, or personal preferences.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-10.proposition: Atheism by itself supplies no moral system, while abandoning Christianity's story of God becoming weak risks greater social callousness toward vulnerable and powerless people.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: Atheism alone supplies no positive social program, while secular-humanist values held by some atheists can contribute constructively to a better world.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: Intolerant exclusion and punitive political dogmatism arise from human ideologies and behavior rather than from atheism as their foundation.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: Reported benefits of religiosity may derive from self-reporting pressures and supportive community rather than religious truth, and secular organizations can reproduce the community mechanism.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: Secular humanism can sustain awe, commitments beyond oneself, social concern, and community without either supernatural belief or coercive state atheism.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: Secular humanism can inherit valuable ideas from Christianity and other traditions while discarding supernatural claims and harmful scriptural baggage because humans transmit and revise moral ideas.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: Appealing to God does not resolve why anyone should care about morality, whereas demonstrable human concern and well-being provide a more direct basis without unsupported theological assumptions.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: Secular humanism offers no guarantee of a better world but improves comparatively by centering human interests, retaining useful inherited ideas, and rejecting harmful doctrines such as biblical slavery.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-03.proposition: A workable moral system can begin from shared concern for human beings and deliberate from that agreement, while an undemonstrated divine premise prevents common inquiry from getting started.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-04.proposition: Human lives can have immense value to human beings without possessing an intrinsic value conferred by the universe or a divine source.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-05.proposition: Consequences for shared well-being make oppressive and exclusionary systems morally assessable even though secular judgments remain corrigible and may later prove mistaken.
